questions.question: What is the primary limitation of a 32-bit word size regarding memory addressing?
options: It can only address 4 gigabytes of memory.
It can only address 20 exabytes of memory.
It requires linear time to access any memory location.
questions.answer: It can only address 4 gigabytes of memory.
questions.explanation: With 32 bits, you can address 2^32 distinct locations, which equals approximately 4 gigabytes.
questions.flashcard_front: What is the memory addressing limit of a 32-bit word size?
questions.flashcard_explanation: A 32-bit word allows for 2^32 unique addresses, resulting in a 4GB limit.

questions.question: In the Word RAM model, memory is accessed in constant time.
questions.explanation: The fundamental assumption of the Word RAM model is that random access to any memory location occurs in constant time.
questions.flashcard_front: True or False: Word RAM assumes constant time memory access.
questions.flashcard_explanation: Random access memory implies that any location can be accessed in constant time.

questions.question: What does it mean for a computer to be 'byte addressable'?
questions.answer: It means there is a unique address for every consecutive eight-bit chunk in memory.
questions.explanation: Modern computers do not address individual bits; they address collections of eight bits, known as bytes.
questions.flashcard_back: Each unique address refers to a consecutive eight-bit chunk of memory.
questions.flashcard_explanation: Computers address memory in bytes (8 bits) rather than individual bits.

questions.question: Why does operating on a linear amount of memory take linear time in the Word RAM model?
questions.answer: Because the CPU can only operate on a constant amount of memory in constant time, so processing linear data requires a linear number of constant-time operations.
questions.explanation: Since each operation is limited to a constant amount of data, scaling the data to size n requires n operations.
questions.flashcard_front: Why is operating on linear memory linear time?
questions.flashcard_back: The CPU processes a constant amount of memory in constant time per operation.
questions.flashcard_explanation: Because each operation is constant-time and constant-size, processing n items requires n operations.
